RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Senior Backend Engineer | Python, Go
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 21 years of experience building production services and large-scale distributed systems in Python, Go and C++. Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service handling 120k requests per second, and led technical work on a playback API and a migration from a Python 2 monolith to around 60 Python and Go services. Experienced with PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform and observability tooling. Fluent in English and experienced in documenting architecture and explaining technical trade-offs.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH, Munich
2019 – August 2026
- Led the technical migration of a Python 2 monolith into approximately 60 Python and Go services deployed on GKE; playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Established a service template using Python/FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and Terraform modules.
- Led the platform organisation responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
- Built an internal cost dashboard using Python, BigQuery billing exports and Looker Studio; rightsizing and committed-use discounts reduced cloud spend by 31% (€4.2M per year).
- Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.

Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH
2015 – 2019
- Led technical work on the playback API, using Python, Tornado and an internal framework similar to FastAPI, with Cassandra and Redis.
- Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service for subscriptions, regions and devices; it handled peak traffic of 120k requests per second with p99 latency under 15 ms.
- Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.

Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart
2010 – 2015
- Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
- Led a team of six developers on the route-history product.
- Co-inventor of a granted patent for adaptive GPS sampling in vehicle fleets.

Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe
2005 – 2010
- Developed C++ and Python software for industrial data acquisition on Linux and embedded x86.
- Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.

SELECTED PROJECTS & OPEN SOURCE
- Open-source maintainer, Python retry library (2012–2018): Maintained a library with approximately 1.5k GitHub stars; used pytest and tox.
- Entitlement Service (Streamhaus, 2016–2017): Go, gRPC, Cassandra, Redis and Kubernetes; 120k requests per second at peak.
- Monolith to Services Migration (Streamhaus, 2019–2023): Python, FastAPI, Go, GKE, Terraform, OpenTelemetry and Prometheus.

EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent to MSc), Computer Science | Rhine Valley University, 2005

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, Go, C++
Backend and APIs: FastAPI, Django, Flask, Tornado, asyncio, REST APIs, gRPC, Protobuf
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL, PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), Kubernetes, Terraform; AWS (EC2, S3)
Testing and observability: pytest, tox, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management

LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)

PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
- “Running Python at 100k rps” — conference talk, 2018
- “Cost is a feature” — internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, professional, and highly achievement-oriented. It presents strong evidence of large-scale backend engineering, Python and Go services, cloud deployment, distributed systems, observability, and technical leadership. The quantified results—120k requests per second, p99 latency under 15 ms, 99.5% to 99.95% availability, and €4.2M annual savings—create strong impact. The main content weakness is role targeting: the document still gives substantial prominence to director-level leadership even though the target role is a hands-on Backend Engineer position. It also does not clearly distinguish recent hands-on Python work from earlier experience. Some requested areas, such as PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, Docker, and CI/CD, are not evidenced in the candidate information and should not be implied.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses conventional section headings, reverse chronology, readable bullet points, standard date formats, and strong keyword coverage for Python, Go, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and cloud deployment. It should parse well in most ATS platforms, with a high but not perfect AI-screening probability because the experience is senior and relevant but several exact must-have terms are either unsupported or absent: Docker, CI/CD, REST API design/consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning, and schema migrations. The phrase "internal framework similar to FastAPI" is understandable to a human but less useful for automated screening than the supported, precise technologies already listed elsewhere. Remove the unsupported REST APIs claim rather than retaining a keyword that is not substantiated by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for the production-backend, Python/Go, cloud, reliability, architecture, observability, Kafka, Kubernetes, and Terraform aspects of the role. The fleet-telematics experience provides relevant transport-domain exposure, while the playback and entitlement services demonstrate performance and reliability work at substantially larger scale than the advertised tracking API. English communication and explaining technical trade-offs are supported by the summary, architecture documentation, RFC process, talks, and architecture-review experience. The main alignment gaps are Docker, CI/CD, explicit REST API design or consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning, and safe schema migrations; the original candidate information does not establish these capabilities, so they should not be added through rewriting. Dutch and French are also not listed. The CV may appear more senior and leadership-oriented than the target role, but its technical depth and explicit Senior Backend Engineer heading help mitigate that concern.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary section and the Technical Skills section, remove the unsupported claim "REST APIs." Replace it with truthful wording such as "backend APIs" in the summary, and retain the supported API technologies "FastAPI," "gRPC," and "Protobuf" in the skills section. Do not describe the APIs as REST unless the candidate can substantiate that experience.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary section, make the hands-on backend focus more prominent by changing the opening to something like: "Senior backend engineer with 21 years of experience building production services and large-scale distributed systems in Python, Go, and C++." Keep the quantified entitlement-service, migration, and availability results immediately afterward. This better targets the advertised Backend Engineer role without adding unsupported experience.

MINOR — In the Professional Experience section under Director of Engineering, Platform, keep the leadership scope but place the technical accomplishments before organisational responsibilities. For example, retain the migration, service-template, and cost-dashboard bullets first, then the platform-organisation and RFC/on-call bullets. This makes the CV's engineering relevance more visible to a recruiter screening for a hands-on backend role.

MINOR — In the Principal Engineer section, explicitly retain the supported API and persistence technologies in the first two bullets, for example: "Led technical work on the playback API using Python and Tornado, with Cassandra and Redis" and "Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service using gRPC, Cassandra, Redis, and Kubernetes." This improves keyword clarity without claiming unsupported REST experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential hallucination: the CV claims experience with "REST APIs" in both the Professional Summary and Technical Skills sections, but the Original Candidate Information does not substantiate REST API design or consumption. This must be removed or replaced with supported API terminology. The CV does not hallucinate Docker, CI/CD, PostgreSQL query tuning, or schema migrations; those are unsupported gaps rather than claims in the document.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "REST APIs" (listed in the professional summary and technical skills); the candidate's material supports API work but does not specifically establish REST API experience.
- "explaining technical trade-offs"; the candidate's material supports architecture reviews and documentation, but not this specific communication experience.
unsupported_claims: "REST APIs" (listed in the professional summary and technical skills); the candidate's material supports API work but does not specifically establish REST API experience.
"explaining technical trade-offs"; the candidate's material supports architecture reviews and documentation, but not this specific communication experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with substantial quantified impact, clear career progression, and credible technical depth. The entitlement service, migration, availability, traffic, latency, fleet-ingestion, and cloud-cost metrics make the experience persuasive. The document is also appropriately reframed toward a senior backend role rather than presenting the candidate only as an engineering leader. The main content limitation is that several requirements are only partially evidenced: REST API design and consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, Docker, and CI/CD. The CV also presents broad leadership and platform ownership that may make the candidate appear more senior and management-oriented than the target role, although the Senior Backend Engineer headline helps mitigate this.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text contact details, and ATS-friendly keyword sections. It includes strong matches such as Python, FastAPI, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, GKE, pytest, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and cloud deployment. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the general Python backend, distributed systems, cloud, Kubernetes, and observability portions of the role. Screening probability is weaker for the exact must-have terms Docker, REST APIs, schema migrations, query tuning, and CI/CD because they are not supported by the candidate information and therefore should not be added. The phrase “internal framework similar to FastAPI” is slightly awkward and may create ambiguity; the CV should distinguish the actual technology from the comparison.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate is a very strong match for Python/backend services, cloud deployment, Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka, observability, automated testing, technical design, and production reliability. The fleet-telematics work provides relevant transport-domain experience, although it is not the same as shipment tracking or logistics software. English fluency and architecture documentation support the communication requirement. The candidate's scale and leadership background substantially exceed the role's minimum experience level, but the CV does not fully demonstrate recent hands-on work in all of the advertised technologies. Docker, REST API design/consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning, live-data schema migrations, and CI/CD are not supported in the original candidate information and are therefore genuine requirement gaps rather than CV-writing defects. Dutch and French are also not listed among the candidate's languages.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR BUT MEANINGFUL ATS/ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the sentence beginning “Experienced with PostgreSQL...” with a more requirement-focused version using only supported evidence: “Experienced building Python and Go backend services, deploying production services on GKE, and working with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, pytest/tox, and Prometheus/OpenTelemetry observability.” This makes backend services, cloud deployment, automated testing, and observability more explicit without adding unsupported Docker, REST, or CI/CD claims.
2. In Technical Skills, change the heading “Testing and observability” to “Automated Testing and Observability,” retaining “pytest, tox, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry.” This uses the job description’s terminology while remaining truthful.
3. In the Professional Experience section under “Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG,” revise the fleet-telematics bullet to: “Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.” Retain the existing wording if desired, but ensure “backend systems,” “ingestion,” and “PostgreSQL” remain close together for ATS matching.
4. In the Professional Experience section under “Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems,” revise the testing bullet to: “Built a Python automated test harness used by QA for eight years.” This is directly supported by the original candidate information and makes the automated-testing evidence more searchable.
5. In the Selected Projects & Open Source section, keep the retry-library entry but change “Maintained a library with approximately 1.5k GitHub stars; used pytest and tox” to “Maintained an open-source Python retry library with approximately 1.5k GitHub stars; used pytest and tox for automated testing.” This strengthens evidence for the testing requirement without implying CI/CD.
6. In the Principal Engineer experience entry, replace “with Python, Tornado and an internal framework similar to FastAPI” with “using Python and Tornado, alongside an internal web framework.” The current comparison to FastAPI is potentially confusing and should not imply that FastAPI was used for the playback API unless that is specifically true. Keep FastAPI associated with the service template and migration, where the candidate information supports it.
7. In the Professional Summary or the first Selected Projects entry, retain the concrete entitlement-service scale and latency figures, but ensure the wording remains “Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service...” rather than implying that the candidate personally implemented the entire service. The current wording is already acceptable, but this is the strongest evidence of hands-on backend engineering and should remain prominent.
